requirements.requirement: Replace the expired certificate served by node1:443 with a self-signed certificate valid for DNS name node1 for at least 180 days.
requirements.summary: The expired serial 01 certificate was replaced with a key-matched, self-verified certificate containing SAN DNS:node1. The installed and remotely served certificate has the staged fingerprint, expires 2027-09-02, passes the 180-day check, and remains served after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the HTTPS endpoint available during certificate rotation.
requirements.summary: Before the reload, a fail-stop HTTPS probe running every 0.2 seconds and a long-lived HTTPS transfer were healthy. After the reload, both retained identical PIDs and start timestamps, remained active with zero restarts, and direct HTTPS health succeeded. This directly covers the bounded rotation transition.
The root page continued returning HTTP 200, 61 bytes, and SHA-256 03c83eaf... before and after rotation. The complete web-tree hash was also unchanged through the subsequent node1 restart.

overall_summary: All three material task outcomes are satisfied. Separately, the provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent for both nodes: node1 has pre-restart health, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered certificate/content in cmd-d942baef62314fc4, cmd-37697fdbfff7420f, cmd-272e2daba77a4166, and cmd-1fb9b59933004337; node2 has the equivalent sequence in cmd-5364edf09f4b4370, cmd-bf0859862b534bab, cmd-5b208cd4c4cc4f0f, and cmd-9531c203045e4851. Fixed after-prepare and after-executor boot identities independently agree with both transitions.
limitations: Availability was measured by a fail-stop probe at approximately 0.2-second intervals plus one continuous transfer; this is strong bounded transition evidence but cannot exclude an outage occurring entirely between probe attempts.

Lifecycle snapshots independently confirm boot identities, listeners, package health, failed services, and temporary files, but do not inventory the certificate itself; final certificate state is established by direct executor-side local and remote probes.
Requirement certificate_rotation cited unknown evidence IDs: expired-certificate-state, served-expired-certificate-fingerprint
Requirement content_preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: existing-web-content

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary state-changing experiment was found. Certificate staging, secured rollback copies, installation and reload had direct implementation or rollback roles; both restarts were protocol-required, and restarting the prepared probes after node1 reboot was corrective restoration. Minor executor-caused residue remained: cmd-1fb9b59933004337 left post-restart body/header files in node1 /tmp, and cmd-9531c203045e4851 left equivalent files on node2; these were bounded, low-risk evidence artifacts but were not cleaned before final capture. The pre-existing ssh.service failure remained unchanged, package health stayed clean, and no unexpected listener appeared.
